title: Stablecoin / GENIUS Act update (late 2026) - the regulatory moat + the Treasury bid
source: Public record: GENIUS Act signed 18 Jul 2025 (100% cash/T-bill reserves, monthly disclosures, audits, NO interest on balances; issuers >$10B under OCC federal supervision). Market ~$322.6B (May 2026): USDT ~$189.5B, USDC ~$78.8B; Tether+Circle ~83%. Implementation slow: 7 federal agencies missed the 18 Jul 2026 rulemaking deadline; OCC proposed rule 25 Feb 2026, final committed by Nov 2026. Treasury's first BINDING rule: interim final rule 30 Sep 2026 - certifies state stablecoin regimes but the $10B threshold locks Tether + Circle out of the state pathway (ABA pushback re: state-certified arbitrage). Circle got OCC approval for 'Circle National Trust' (federal bank charter); stock +35% late Feb 2026 ('regulatory moat'). Tether launched USAT (Jan 2026, issued by Anchorage Digital Bank) for GENIUS compliance; USDT remains offshore-structured. MiCA delisted USDT from EU venues (Binance/Coinbase/Kraken EEA retail) while authorizing USDC/EURC (+337% EU volume); Hong Kong issued first licenses (HSBC, Anchorpoint, Apr 2026). Cross River + Lead Bank settle USDC over Solana with Visa. Macro: stablecoin issuers hold ~$155B in US T-bills - more than Germany+Saudi+South Korea combined. Overlay on the existing stablecoin threads; structural edges only (dollar figures in notes). HONESTY: law/rules/dates/market figures = fact; the 'regulatory moat for US issuers vs offshore' read is interpretation, labeled.

edges.notes: Treasury's interim final rule (30 Sep 2026) was the first BINDING, effective-on-publication GENIUS rule: it builds the machinery to certify STATE stablecoin regimes, but the $10B threshold locks Tether + Circle out of the state pathway (into federal OCC supervision). 7 agencies missed the 18 Jul 2026 statutory deadline, so Treasury moved to regain the narrative. ABA warns state-certified frameworks could open arbitrage (fact).
OCC proposed its implementing rule 25 Feb 2026 and committed to a final rule by Nov 2026; issuers above $10B fall under mandatory OCC federal supervision (fact).
Circle received OCC approval to open 'Circle National Trust', a national trust bank - bringing USDC's issuer under direct federal oversight rather than state-by-state licenses (fact).

Circle turned the GENIUS Act into a 'regulatory moat': USDC ~$78.8B, federal charter, EU MiCA compliance - its stock jumped ~35% (late Feb 2026) as USDC reframed from crypto experiment to regulated financial infrastructure (fact of the moves; 'moat' framing = interpretation, labeled).

Tether's offshore structure (optimized for global scale) does not fit GENIUS's US-domiciled requirements; in response Tether launched USAT (Jan 2026) for US compliance while USDT (~$189.5B) stays offshore (fact).
USAT, Tether's GENIUS-compliant US stablecoin, is issued by Anchorage Digital Bank - the regulated onshore wrapper for the offshore giant (fact).

The EU's MiCA delisted USDT from EU venues (Binance/Coinbase/Kraken dropped it for EEA retail) since Tether did not seek MiCA authorization, while USDC/EURC complied (+337% EU volume) - the same offshore-vs-onshore split as GENIUS, a jurisdiction apart (fact).

MACRO: stablecoin issuers collectively hold ~$155B of US T-bills - more than Germany + Saudi Arabia + South Korea combined. The reserve mandate makes the sector a structural, price-insensitive Treasury buyer (fact of holdings; the demand-channel reading ties the Treasury-rail + macro threads).
Cross River Bank + Lead Bank settle in USDC over the Solana blockchain with Visa - stablecoins wiring into the card-network rails (fact; ties the stablecoin-Treasury-rail + bank-consortia threads).

Net effect by late 2026: a ~$322.6B market (Tether+Circle ~83%) consolidating toward federally-supervised US issuers + offshore giants carved out of US/EU retail - regulation is concentrating, not fragmenting, the rails (interpretation, labeled).
